view: Macro three-quarter detail of a single-button barrel cuff shown unbuttoned and curled open (matching the tech-pack pose): the bias-cut inner facing turned toward camera and dominant, outer cuff face with its button and the lower sleeve in frame for straight-grain stripe comparison; collar and body out of frame.

geometry.cuff_type: single-button rounded-corner barrel cuff, drawn unbuttoned and curled open into a cylinder
geometry.bias_component: ENTIRE inner cuff facing, cut on the true bias at 45 degrees to the fabric grain (marked in the blueprint by red 45-degree hatching across the exposed inner face)
geometry.straight_grain_components: outer cuff face, sleeve, sleeve placket — all stripes on straight grain, running down the sleeve and perpendicular to the cuff's long edges
geometry.button: exactly one 4-hole button on the outer face, centered in the cuff depth, with a hand-wrapped thread shank (as drawn)
geometry.corner: front cuff corner softly rounded (round-cut), wide gentle curve as drawn — not square, not beveled
geometry.stitching: single row of edge topstitching 6 mm inside every cuff edge, drawn as dashed lines on the outer face and echoed on the inner facing; upper solid line is the cuff-to-sleeve attachment seam
geometry.panel_integrity: outer cuff face is ONE uninterrupted panel; its only seams are the sleeve attachment seam and the perimeter edge topstitching (failure-log lesson: forbid invented mid-panel seams)

ratios: cuff depth = ~6 x button diameter (6.5 cm vs 10.5 mm button)
edge topstitch offset = ~0.5 x button diameter (6 mm), so the button rim reads clearly wider than the stitch margin
bias stripes cross the straight-grain stripes at exactly 45 degrees where inner facing meets outer edge
bias facing fills 100% of the inner cuff depth — full-depth facing, not a partial trim strip
locked_features: Fine blue-and-white bengal-striped shirting (approx 2 mm blue stripes on white); bias is INVISIBLE on solids so stripes are mandatory
Inner cuff facing stripes run diagonally at exactly 45 degrees; outer cuff, sleeve and placket stripes run straight — never diagonal on any outer part, never straight on the inner facing
Same identical stripe fabric inside and out, rotated 45 degrees — not a contrast fabric, not a different color, not a print
Exactly ONE button (four holes, thread shank) — one button, not two; no convertible, French, or link cuff
Rounded front cuff corner exactly as drawn
Single 6 mm edge topstitch row around the full cuff perimeter
Cuff shown unbuttoned and turned open so the inner facing faces the camera
No annotation text, arrows, numbers, or red hatch lines may leak into the photo; the red hatching is a grain-direction marker only
distinguishing_vs_siblings: bias-none: stripes straight-grain EVERYWHERE, zero diagonal. bias-inner-collar-stand: diagonal stripes appear only on the inside of the collar band at the neck (collar shot). bias-inner-top-collar: diagonal stripes appear only on the flipped-up collar underside (collar shot). bias-inner-cuff (THIS option): the only diagonal-stripe component anywhere is the inner cuff facing, revealed by the opened cuff; the collar is out of frame entirely.
uncertain: Exact rounded-corner radius — drawing is stylized; ~1.5 cm assumed
Cuff depth not dimensioned in the tech pack; standard 6.5 cm barrel depth assumed
Upper solid line in the blueprint read as the cuff-to-sleeve attachment seam (could alternatively be the overlap edge of the closed cuff)
Stripe scale is a category convention (fine bengal ~2 mm), not specified by the drawing
